page: Amazon Web Services c8g.4xlarge is an ARM-based compute-optimized instance hosted on the AWS Nitro system. It is powered by an AWS Neoverse-V2 processor using the ARMv9 architecture, operating at 2.8 GHz across 16 dedicated physical cores with 16 vCPUs and no simultaneous multithreading. Each core includes 64 KB of L1 data cache and 2 MB of L2 cache, backed by 36 MB of shared L3 cache. System memory totals 32.0 GB, providing a standard compute-optimized memory-to-vCPU allocation of 2.0 GB per core. The instance provides an 8 Gbps baseline network bandwidth, lacks local instance storage, and does not include graphics acceleration hardware.

Benchmark testing demonstrates notable memory subsystem throughput and data processing capability. In PassMark memory benchmarks, the instance achieves top-tier results in the top 10 percent with a score of 3108.83, supported by strong uncached memory read bandwidth of 302.31 GB/sec and write bandwidth of 123.66 GB/sec. Data manipulation is similarly strong, with bzip3 multi-threaded decompression reaching 201.27 GB/sec and PassMark database operations scoring 24008.08, both landing in the top quartile. General compute throughput remains squarely within the middle 50 percent, registering a Geekbench 6 multi-core score of 15870.0 and a multi-core stress-ng metric of 27286.64.

Hardware tradeoffs center around memory density, storage architecture, and large-model machine learning. With 32.0 GB of RAM across 16 cores, the platform trades large in-memory capacities for high per-core execution efficiency. The lack of integrated local NVMe storage requires reliance on network-attached volumes for persistence, while LLM prompt processing for medium 7B models falls into the bottom quartile at 31.15 tokens per second due to the absence of dedicated tensor acceleration.

In terms of qualitative efficiency, the Neoverse-V2 architecture offers robust compute throughput per watt and per core compared to legacy x86 architectures without hyperthreading overhead. It is best applied to compute-bound pipelines such as Clang software compilation, containerized microservices, distributed data decompression, static web delivery, and caching engines such as Redis.
description: Amazon Web Services c8g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by a 16-core AWS Neoverse-V2 ARMv9 processor clocked at 2.8 GHz. Featuring 16 dedicated single-threaded vCPUs and 32.0 GB of memory, it provides a 1:2 core-to-memory ratio designed for compute-centric applications. The server features no local NVMe storage and no GPU acceleration, relying on network-attached storage and an 8 Gbps network baseline. Performance benchmarks highlight an exceptional memory subsystem, reaching the top 10 percent in PassMark memory testing and top quartile in uncached read and write bandwidth. Compression decompression throughput and database operations are also strong, while general-purpose multi-core CPU metrics fall into the median tier. Lacking hardware matrix accelerators, large model prompt processing is limited. The instance delivers solid qualitative cost-performance for distributed microservices, CI/CD compilation, high-throughput caching, and data batch processing workloads.
